text:
Connor McDavid had found the scoresheet in 23 straight games. The Edmonton Oilers had won six in a row. Andrei Vasilevskiy ended both on Thursday, stopping 23 of 24 shots as the Tampa Bay Lightning won 3-1.

This was a strange game to read off the shot counts alone. Edmonton had more attempts, 54 to 45, and more shots on goal, but at even strength Tampa's chances were far better: 2.65 expected goals to 1.32 (expected goals measure the quality of chances, not just the volume). Daily Faceoff Edmonton's pregame line called Tampa "ruthless at 5-on-5," and this looked like it. Edmonton also gave the puck away 20 times to Tampa's 8.

The second period belonged to Tampa, 1.62 expected goals to 0.64, and that's where it broke open. Devon Levi stopped Anthony Cirelli on a 28% chance, but on the power play at 13:29 John Carlson, in his first season with Tampa after signing as a free agent in July, beat Levi with a slap shot. Our win chance for the Lightning jumped from 55% to 75% on that goal.

Edmonton went 0 for 3 on the power play, and the third period was where the gap showed. Ilya Mikheyev scored on a slap shot at 10:46 and Nikita Kucherov added another at 14:29 before Colton Dach tipped in a late one for Edmonton. Levi, who had won 10 of his previous 11 starts since arriving from Buffalo, wasn't the problem; he finished slightly above what his shots deserved. Vasilevskiy, at 1.57 goals saved above expected, was the difference, and he added the most wins of anyone on the ice.

The Oilers still sit second in the league with 37 points; Minnesota leads with 38. The bigger question in Edmonton is Mike Babcock's decision to split McDavid and Leon Draisaitl onto separate lines, which drew plenty of coverage this week. On a night when the two combined for no goals, that debate will only get louder.
headline: Vasilevskiy ends McDavid's streak and the Oilers' run
